paper.title: PTM-VQA: Efficient Video Quality Assessment Leveraging Diverse PreTrained Models from the Wild
paper.page_convention: 1-based PDF pages; printed page 2835 is PDF p.1

text_evidence_sources: Rendered PDF pages and verified crops

claims.claim: Frozen features from distinct pretraining tasks provide different quality cues.

evidence.note: DBI varies across models under MOS-informed feature analysis.

caveats: LMNN and labels influence the analysis; visualization is not label-free proof.

claims.claim: The model trains adapters and a head while keeping backbones frozen.

evidence.note: 128-dimensional adapters with two fully connected layers.

caveats: Frozen backbone inference is still required.

claims.claim: ICID aligns model views and separates quality groups through centroids.
caveats: Printed Eq.3 uses ordered pairs and a factor 2; exact scaling needs code verification.

claims.claim: Inverse DBI weights favor compact separated quality groups.

evidence.note: Lower scatter/separation ratio gives higher inverse weight.

caveats: Selection threshold and split separation insufficiently specified.

claims.claim: Training cost is low for the chosen adapters and sampled setup.
caveats: Not total deployed model parameters or pretraining cost.

claims.claim: Weighted mean is competitive but not every benchmark is won.
LSVQ supports adapting selected combinations on larger labeled data.
caveats: Suffixes identify combinations, not zero-shot source training.

evidence.note: KoNViD improves over PVQ; LIVE-VQC best PTM 0.7852/0.7367 below PVQ 0.807/0.770.

claims.claim: ICID improves reported KoNViD ablation correlations.
caveats: No comparison with all metric-learning alternatives.

claims.claim: Six-bin configuration is better in the displayed ablation.

evidence.note: Six bins outperform two and four.

caveats: Bin count and boundaries vary together.

claims.claim: DBI weighting improves two datasets but LIVE-VQC is mixed.

evidence.note: LIVE PLCC decreases while SRCC increases slightly.

claims.claim: PLCC and SRCC mathematically range from −1 to 1.
caveats: Observed useful correlations in the tables are positive.
